priceSnapshot.note: THE HAWKISH-HOLD FADE DID NOT FOLLOW THROUGH. Endday handed over at $63,727 with price bleeding under the $64,000 shelf and a bearish tilt built on two pillars - a fifth straight ETF outflow day and an AI-capex de-rating hammering QQQ. BOTH pillars broke overnight. Microsoft reported after the close, jumped ~9% after hours and CUT its 2026 capex guide to $175B from $190B, which is exactly the reassurance the Nasdaq had been demanding; Meta fell ~7% on a weak Q2 and a raised capex floor, but the net read on US futures was risk-ON. And Farside's FINAL Jul 29 print came in at +$32.1M NET INFLOW (IBIT +89.8, FBTC -43.1, ARKB -14.6) - not the -$57.7M preliminary endday used. BTC rallied off $63,611 to tag $64,393.2 at 02:19 COT, stopping the desk's small overnight hedge, then faded back to $64,043. Working against the reclaim: DXY firmed to 101.02, US10Y sits at 4.688% (+0.066 vs the 4.622% prior close, still a year high), and Brent added another $1.43 to $92.17 - an energy-inflation impulse six hours ahead of Q2 GDP and core PCE at 08:30 ET.

Below $63,000 the ladder is thin - $62,684 (the Jul 28 flush low) then the $62,200 structural invalidation - and the realized-liquidation book shows almost nothing resting between $63,000 and $63,500 to slow it down.

What changed, in order of weight: (1) the ETF outflow streak is DEAD - Jul 29 finalised at +$32.1M with BlackRock's IBIT buying $89.8M, breaking a four-day, -$526.5M run; (2) Microsoft's capex CUT to $175B removed the single loudest bear argument in the equity complex and flipped US futures higher; (3) BTC held the $63,611 low and pushed to $64,393, and the 4H MACD histogram has crossed POSITIVE (+30.82) for the first time since the FOMC fade. What did NOT change: price is still below every daily EMA (20/50/100/200), the $64,350-$64,500 cap rejected again, DXY and Brent both firmed, and OKX's long/short account ratio is back to 1.58 - retail is long again into an inflation print. So the add is deliberately SMALL and the $63,000 reduce rail plus the $61,900 resting stop both stay live. Probabilities move to bull 30 / range 45 / bear 25.

earnings.note: Microsoft's fiscal Q4 beat, Azure outran expectations on cloud and AI demand, and - the part that actually moved the complex - it CUT calendar-2026 capex guidance to $175B from $190B. The AI-capex de-rating that took QQQ to $661.73, its cheapest close of the month, was built on the fear that hyperscaler spending was running away. Microsoft just argued the opposite. US equity futures turned higher on it.

Meta's Q2 missed and Q3 guidance came in light, and it RAISED the floor of its 2026 capex range to $130-145B from $125-145B - the mirror image of Microsoft's message. The market rewarded discipline and punished spending, which tells you what the tape currently cares about. Net across the two: futures higher, but the Nasdaq's internals are being sorted rather than lifted.

earnings.reaction: pending - 08:30 ET today, inside the morning session's window
earnings.note: Q2 GDP and core PCE both land at 08:30 ET, roughly six hours after this report. After Wednesday's 9-3 hold with Hammack, Kashkari and Logan dissenting FOR an immediate hike, a hot core-PCE print is the fastest route to September-hike pricing and the $62,000 zone; a cool one is the cleanest path to closing above $64,500. Brent at $92.17 and the 10Y at 4.688% are both leaning toward the hot side. The Bank of England also decides today.

Apple (fiscal Q3) and Amazon (Q2) report after the Jul 30 close, so mega-cap earnings risk runs through the midday and endday sessions too. With Microsoft and Meta having split the tape, these two decide whether the capex-discipline trade holds. BTC has been tracking Nasdaq beta closely all week, so this is a crypto input, not just an equity one.

calibration.note: Two honest marks against endday. First, its ACTION: the $33 3x short hedge opened at $63,727 with a $64,350 stop was tagged when price printed $64,393.2 at 02:19 COT, so it stopped out for a small loss - acting did not help. It was still a defensible trade at the time (crowded longs, five apparent outflow days, a stacked overnight calendar) and the sizing did its job: the damage is about a third of a dollar, not a wound. Second, its ANALYSIS: the bearish tilt leaned on a preliminary -$57.7M ETF number that finalised at +$32.1M, and on an AI-capex fear that Microsoft's guidance cut directly contradicted hours later. The lesson is not 'do not hedge' - it is that a tilt built on same-day preliminary flow data and on an un-reported earnings print is a tilt built on two things that can both be revised overnight. The reduce level itself was right: it did not fire, and price never came close.
